incident-bot: PAGER DUTY ALERT: PD-6789 -> KV_PREFETCH regression detected in prod-west. Elevated cache eviction rates, continuous-batching throughput drop, and 99th pct tail latency spike. Auto-tags: kv-cache, batching, scheduler, p1. Link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/kv-prefetch

Maria (oncall-sre): I'm on it. Seeing 99th ↑ from ~180ms -> ~1.2s across model-pool-3. Error rates for small/short requests up ~6% (upstream timeouts). Customers on dedicated capacity seeing increased tail latency. Paging eng-runtime and eng-platform.

Alex (eng-runtime): ack. I noticed the kv-prefetch change from the last runtime deploy (runt-2026-03-14) adjusted prefetch window heuristics. Hypothesis: prefetch aggression plus continuous batching kept long-running requests in long-lived batches, blowing up KV working set and causing eviction storms that then trigger prefix cache repopulation costs. Also mixing lots of long requests with many short ones is starving small requests in the batch scheduler.

Jamal (eng-platform): Confirmed memory pressure on many GPU nodes in prod-west. Node-level OOM attempts and repeated cache eviction logs:

```
[2026-03-14T22:15:03Z] kv_cache.cpp: evicting 128 entries (working_set=1.8GB -> threshold=1.6GB)
[2026-03-14T22:15:03Z] batch_scheduler.cpp: suspended small-worker-queue due to high-headroom
[2026-03-14T22:15:04Z] kv_prefetch.cpp: prefetching prefix id=0x7f2a (cost=12ms) -> exceeded expected
```

Maria (oncall-sre): Immediate mitigation ideas?

Alex (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation: 1) toggle `kv_prefetch.enabled=false` in the runtime config for prod-west pool; 2) cap `max_batch_size` to 8 for mixed-workload routes; 3) enable `fairness_weights=true` experimental flag to prefer small/short requests. These are config flips, no model rollback needed.

Maria (oncall-sre): Jamal can you push the runtime config change? I'll coordinate customer comms.

Jamal (eng-platform): Running the rollout now. Command: 

```
rdwctl config set --pool prod-west --key kv_prefetch.enabled --value false && 
rdwctl config set --pool prod-west --key batch.max_batch_size --value 8
```

Jamal (eng-platform): Output: 

```
Applying config to pool prod-west... OK (20 hosts updated)
Restarting runtime agents (rolling) ... OK
New config verified via /configs endpoint
```

incident-bot: ACTION TAKEN: Config toggles applied to prod-west. Auto-notification sent to PD-6789 subscribers.

Sophia (product): Which customers are affected? Any SLA breaches expected? Need a brief we can send to account teams.

Maria (oncall-sre): Affected: 3 dedicated customers (acct-A, acct-C, acct-F) and a handful of hosted routes (low volume). We currently see SLO degradation on tail latency; no 5xx waterfall at scale but some timeouts reported by client SDKs. Estimating potential SLA exposure window ~20-40m before configs stable. I'll draft a message.

Alex (eng-runtime): Early telemetry: 95th went from 520ms -> 230ms after toggles; 99th from 1.2s -> 420ms. KV eviction rate dropped 4x in the last 7m. Looks positive but still watching for oscillation.

Maria (oncall-sre): Moving to handoff. Summary for night:
- Incident: KV prefetch heuristics + continuous batching causing working set blowups; mixed long/short requests caused starvation of short requests and tail lat spikes.
- Mitigation applied: `kv_prefetch.enabled=false`, `batch.max_batch_size=8` rolled to prod-west (rolling restart).
- Metrics to watch: kv_evictions(/s), batch_queue_length, 99th latency per-route, OOM retry counts. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/kv-prefetch
- Next steps: eng-runtime to craft a patch: (a) add bounded prefetch budget per-host, (b) introduce fairness tokens in scheduler, (c) add telemetry for prefetch cost per-prefix.
- Customer comms: initial notice sent; follow-up to account teams with ETA in ~30m.

Kevin (oncall-sre-night): taking handoff. Thanks Maria — I have the dashboard open. I'll keep pages open and escalate back if 99th resurges above 800ms or eviction rate doubles. Planned overnight actions: keep reduced batch size for 3h, monitor, and if stable propose gradual re-enable of prefetch in canary with heavily reduced budget.

Alex (eng-runtime): For root-cause follow-up: will open a postmortem ticket and attach traces. Early action items I'm creating: RTT-1121 (prefetch budget), RTT-1122 (scheduler fairness), RTT-1123 (add regress-test for mixed request shapes).

Maria (oncall-sre): Thanks team. If anyone sees customer escalation ping me directly. Tagging @pagerduty-bot to close PD once stability confirmed. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: PD-6789 acknowledged by Kevin. Monitoring status updated to "under investigation".

Alex (eng-runtime): Quick log snippet to capture one of the eviction storms we correlated: 
```
[2026-03-14T22:16:01Z] batch: accepted long-run (seq=2048 tokens) with prefetch=on -> batch wait 480ms
[2026-03-14T22:16:01Z] small-request: waiting behind batch id=0xabc (latency 540ms)
[2026-03-14T22:16:02Z] kv_cache: evicting hot prefixes due to mem_pressure
```

Sophia (product): Noted — I'll prepare account-team notes and set expectation that engineering is doing a config mitigation + follow-up patch.

Maria (oncall-sre): Handoff complete. Kevin, assign if you want a second oncall to rotate in.

Kevin (oncall-sre-night): Will ping Alex if we see any regression. Signing off to standby. :coffee:

incident-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED: PD-6789 -> created incident thread id=inc-2026-03-14-042. Tags: kv-cache, batching, scheduler, handoff. Attachments: grafana snapshot, runtime logs.
